title: Cardinality of an injection between two finite sets
statement: Let s and t be finite sets over the naturals and g a function on the naturals. If g is injective on the members of s and sends every member of s to a member of t, then the size of s is at most the size of t.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.Finset.card_le_of_injOn : ((x0 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x1 : AxNat.Finset) -> ((x2 : ((x2 : AxNat) -> AxNat)) -> ((x3 : ((x3 : AxNat) -> ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x3) Bool.true) -> ((x6 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x4) Bool.true) -> ((x7 : Eq.{1} AxNat (x2 x3) (x2 x4)) -> Eq.{1} AxNat x3 x4)))))) -> ((x4 : ((x4 : AxNat) -> ((x5 : Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x0 x4) Bool.true) -> Eq.{1} Bool (AxNat.Finset.memB x1 (x2 x4)) Bool.true))) -> AxNat.le (AxNat.Finset.card x0) (AxNat.Finset.card x1))))))

evidence.notes: The trusted gate cannot tell a THEOREM's statement is not what its name says: a `card_le_of_injOn` with its two `card`s transposed, an `exists_collision` whose pair need not be DISTINCT, or a `pigeonhole` whose strict inequality points the other way would each be admitted, carry an empty axiom footprint, and pass every other row in this ledger. `nat_prelude/finset_pigeonhole_tests.rs` instantiates each statement at a concrete pair of sets whose cardinalities are computed independently, and pairs every positive with the wrong statement it rules out. Three of its controls are the sharper kind, where a hypothesis cannot be DISCHARGED (`infer` must fail) rather than a conclusion merely being false.

notes: card s IS countRange (memB s) (bound s) by delta, so this lift adds no counting content. What it adds is the SHAPE of the hypotheses: the loose form has to carry Lt i n premises because a (predicate, bound) pair is exactly a pair and nothing connects the two, while on the carrier the domain premise is recoverable and the codomain obligation Lt (g i) (bound t) is DERIVED from membership rather than demanded. Both go through F:nat-finset-lt-bound-of-memb. ADR-1593.
